text:
A patient may need a tracheostomy when their upper airway is blocked or at risk of blocking (from trauma, tumor, swelling, or infection), or when they need prolonged mechanical ventilation and a tube through the neck is safer and more comfortable than one through the mouth. It's also used when a patient can't clear secretions or protect their airway, such as after a stroke or neuromuscular disease, and sometimes during major head and neck surgery or in cases of severe sleep apnea.
